disposition.reason: Python BacktestReadThroughCache alone publishes the coverage row after the versioned cache slice is visible and verifies. An independent Java writer would forge or race this integrity assertion.
disposition.java_surface: READ-only DatasetDefinition, four-field typed mapper and bounded repository with ReadGroup binding.
disposition.write_rejection: DatasetDefinition declares READ only; no Java write, sync or materialization entry point was added.

contract.time_semantics: Exchange business date carried by a UTC-midnight TIMESTAMP; not an event instant.
contract.receipt_semantics: Source version is a SHA-256 fingerprint of the current view and source table/partition state; row_count and content_digest describe one published cache slice at that exact version.

python_owner.publisher: _publish writes cache first, waits for WAL/content visibility, then publishes coverage.
python_owner.reader: _cached requires the exact (trade_date, source_version) receipt and verifies cache count, unique stock keys and pandas content digest.
python_owner.checkpoint: Not a source-ingest checkpoint; no Java checkpoint state applies.

target.reason_no_isolated_write_target: The owner-controlled integrity receipt was validated by SELECT only; no Java writer exists under the retained compatibility decision.

read_acceptance.database_access: Configured local QuestDB over JDBC and Python PGWire; SELECT only.

known_limitations: The stored historical receipt is internally valid, but its source_version is stale relative to the current view/source state. A current-version Python read will cache miss and may publish new cache rows; that writing path was not invoked.
Only the latest existing receipt date and its complete 5,565-row versioned slice were checked, not every historical receipt.
Java intentionally does not publish or repair coverage; Python retains that responsibility.
